The '''2000–01 [[La Liga]]''' season was the 70th since its establishment. It began on 9 September 2000, and concluded on 17 June 2001.

== Teams ==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[1999–2000 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. The promoted teams were [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] and [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], returning to the top flight after an absence of twelve, six and one years respectively. They replaced [[Real Betis|Betis]], [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], ending their top flight spells of six, sixty six and one year respectively. For the first time in 26 years, there was no team from Seville.

== Overall ==
* Most wins – [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (24)
* Fewest wins – [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] and [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] (9)
* Most draws – [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] and [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] (15)
* Fewest draws – [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] and [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] (7)
* Most losses – [[Real Oviedo]], [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] and [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] (19)
* Fewest losses – [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (6)
* Most goals scored – [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (81)
* Fewest goals scored – [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] (40)
* Most goals conceded – [[Real Sociedad]] and [[Rayo Vallecano]] (68)
* Fewest goals conceded – [[Valencia C.F.|Valencia]] (34)

=== Fair Play award ===
[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] was the winner of the Fair-play award with 86 points, second was [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] and third [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]].<ref name="FairPlay">{{cite web|title=Ganadores de los Premios Juego Limpio |trans-title=Fair-play awards Winners |url=http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298#ancla7 |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF]] |access-date=5 September 2010 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407195555/http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298 |archive-date=7 April 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=El Real Madrid, ganador del Premio al Juego Limpio 2003 |trans-title=Real Madrid, 2003 Fair Play Award Winner |url=http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2003/200306/20030626/20030626_6350.shtm |publisher=[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (filed) |access-date=6 September 2010 |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807104903/http://www.noticias.info/Archivo/2003/200306/20030626/20030626_6350.shtm |archive-date=7 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
